bought it for £8.99 on sale because i wanted to have played it before its sequel. 

giving it a negative review because they are price gouging.

6 hour long story on hard. i dont think there is an active multiplayer community

Warhammer 40,000 Space Marine was fun enough to play in the beginning and felt like a chore to finish. Dated gameplay mechanics, Early 2010s shooter AI, and other frustrating experiences. The story is quite weak. Another 40K storyline fluffed out using a McGuffin ala Inquisition. Here's to hoping Space Marine 2 will be more engaging and thrilling. Not Recommended

[h1] KILL DA SPAAACE MARINESSSSS!!! [/h1]

I'll admit that first few hours was boring and the level design, art design etc. looks boring too but at one point I started to have fun with melee + rifle mix but I still didn't know what to expect from the universe and story. (This happened around 2-3hr mark of my playthrough.)

After killing gazillions of Orcs for 4-5 hours I started to feel let down again
then the breaking point happened in the story and at that moment I freaking wished this game's universe had more games in TPS or FPS genre instead of RTS...

Game finally started to give me unique enough enemies because come on man orcs are generic and boring as ♥♥♥♥. At that point your arsenal is kinda complete anyway so it starts to feel fresh again.

I don't have anything else to say about gameplay. It's your classic TPS/Action and it can be fun but it's nothing extremely special.

Let's jump back to Story ; Unfortunately it's not deep enough and some stuff is easily predictable. I don't know why they decided to focus on the classic an army at war but it's almost like it's from real life and not from Warhammer 40K. I think that undermines the story a lot because just a little bit sauce of the universe unveils itself in the breaking point and that is far more interesting than an american-like army killing orcs and there is huge ass armored guys. (Don't get me wrong huge ass armored guys are part of the sauce but game holds on to those details too long and even after that I still don't know too much about it.)

I think this game saves itself by being a part of an universe to be honest. If it wasn't like that this would be so bad but Warhammer's unique parts and fun mixable combat gameplay carries the game not the other parts...

Overall I had fun I wish story was more detailed and more focused on the lore instead of a generic ass war. (Maybe that war is not generic but I'll never know thanks to writers.) Killing enemies with mixing bunch of OP rifles and one OP hammer is very fun to do.

It's a shame that this universe is more connected to RTS genre than TPS/FPS in games. I would love to see more because this game is just a teaser with name drops nothing more...

[h3] 7.5/10 [/h3]

Combat: The combat isn't as quick as I would have liked. The dodge-roll felt unresponsive at times, the transition between ranged and melee isn't as smooth as it likely could have been, and the combos and finishers felt a bit uninspired (though I am very glad that they were kept simple).

Weapons & Gear: The gathering of more weapons and skills was cool, and it was really cool to see some of that progression in the form of the armor gaining more elements to it, but I would have preferred if the changes were a little more noticeable. Additionally, the changing of loadouts felt a bit unintuitive, and most of the time I used only a handful of weapons throughout the whole game: Boltor [spoiler]and Storm Boltor[/spoiler] for heavier enemies, Pistol for trash mobs, Melee for most every other enemy (given that you can only heal with a finisher attack, which is dumb), and Sniping for specialized enemies that were particular nuisances. It was nice to have the option to have other weapon types (shotgun, grenade launcher, alternative rifle), but I found myself ignoring them by the end of the game.
[spoiler]To be more specific, by the end I was only using the Plasma Pistol, Kraken Boltor, Storm Boltor, Lascannon, Power Axe, and occasionally the Thunder Hammer. I would have used the Thunder Hammer exclusively, but you can only utilize the Pistol and primary Boltor with it. I think I would have preferred if the Thunder Hammer was replaced with a smaller weapon of equal power, because I quickly learned that it's best to have access to your full arsenal than half of it.[/spoiler]
In essence, I would have preferred if the game forced you into periodic loadout changes, or if you had one universal loadout that leveled up like the Pistol and primary Boltor do.

Story: As someone who's still mostly an outsider when it comes to 40k, the story was nice and simple and easy to follow. And that's really all it needed to be, in fairness. I liked most characters in the game, really enjoyed the personality of Captain Titus (the player-controlled character), and actually liked the sequel bait at the end. I honestly can't believe it's taken this long to get [b]any[/b] kind of sequel.

Conclusion: It was an enjoyable 6-and-some-change hours, and I would recommend it to people that want to get the feeling of the brighter side of 40k (y'know, brighter relative to the majority of the series).
